actions.reason: C0001 has coherent strong RNA and CNV identity evidence, positive support across all four modalities with moderate internal reproducibility, positive boundaries to all other sets, and no significant set-specific technical association. Retaining it as a discovery-stage candidate is defensible.

C0002 has strong coherent RNA and CNV identity evidence, positive boundaries to all other sets, and no significant set-specific technical association. CT does not support membership and internal reproducibility is lower, but the molecular identity and boundaries remain defensible for downstream validation.

C0003 lacks significant RNA or CNV differentiation, is supported only by WSI with negative CT/RNA/CNV silhouettes, and has no coherent cross-modal identity. No available structural revision resolves this, so the candidate is insufficiently defensible.

C0004 has coherent RNA and CNV identity evidence and positive support across all four modalities with positive boundaries. Significant site and CT-manufacturer imbalance is a concerning competing explanation for part of its structure, but the defining RNA/CNV signal is not CT-derived, so it remains a defensible discovery-stage candidate with this caveat.
